title: Remove Nodes From Linked List
statement:
`head` is the first node of a singly linked list. A node must be deleted when some node later in the list (anywhere after it, not only right after it) holds a strictly larger value.

Delete all such nodes, keep the others in their original order, and return the head of the resulting list.
constraints: The list has between 1 and 10^5 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

A node survives exactly when it is at least as large as everything after it. Checking every later node for every node is O(n²). Scan left to right with a stack of the survivors so far instead: when a new node arrives, every stacked node with a smaller value now has something larger after it, so it can be dropped for good. Those drops always happen from the top, because the stack is non-increasing from bottom to top. At the end the stack holds exactly the survivors, in list order.

## Approach

1. Walk the list with `node`, starting from `head`.
2. While the top of `stack` has a smaller value than `node`, pop it: `node` is a larger value to its right.
3. Push `node`; the stack stays non-increasing from bottom to top.
4. After the walk, link each kept node to the next one in `stack`. The last kept node is the original tail, whose `next` is already `null`.
5. Return `stack[0]`, the new head.

## Example 1, step by step

`head = [5,2,13,3,8]`. Push `5`, push `2` (stack `[5,2]`). `13` pops `2` and `5`, then is pushed: `[13]`. Push `3`: `[13,3]`. `8` pops `3` and is pushed: `[13,8]`. Linking `13` to `8` gives the answer `[13,8]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is pushed once and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack in the worst case (a non-increasing list keeps every node).

## Pitfalls

- Pop only on a strictly smaller top: equal values do not remove each other, so `[1,1,1,1]` stays whole.
- Do not compare a node only with its immediate neighbour; a larger value anywhere to the right removes it.
- The stack is never empty at the end, because the last node always survives.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | survivors so far, values non-increasing from bottom to top |
| `node` | the list node being read |
| `i` | index used to relink consecutive survivors |
